title: IS12:: rate2.c (5.3)

lines.code: Goal: The use of if-else for conditional calculations
float rate1, rate2, interest_rate; /* interest rates in percents */
float annual_interest; /* annual interest in dollars */

lines.explanation: This scanf statement gets two floating point numbers separated by a blank from the user, processes then using %f specifications and places them into variables rate1 and rate2.
We read a floating point value into a floating point variable capital using %f specification
The goal of the conititional statement below is to decide which of the two rates has to be used in our case to calculate interest. The correct value will be assigned to the variable interest_rate
If capital is less than THRESHOLD, the value of capital < THRESHOLD expression will be 1 and "then" part of if will be executed.
This is the "then" part of if - in this part interest_rate will be assigned to rate1 (lower of the two)
If the condition is false, i.e., the capital is greater or equal to the THRESHOLD, the value of capital < THRESHOLD expression will be 0 and "else" part of if will be executed.
This is the "else" part of if - in this part interest_rate will be assigned to rate2 (higher of the two)

lines.code: printf("The rate for $%.2f is %.2f%%\n", capital, interest_rate);
lines.explanation: Here we print the exact rate to be used in further calculations.
This line calculates the value of annual interest

lines.code: printf("Interest %6.2f; New capital %9.2f\n", annual_interest, capital + annual_interest);
lines.explanation: This line prints the final result of the program - the annual interest and the new capital
